title: Pager VFS, database-file, and journal-name accessors

scope.rationale: sqlite3PagerVfs, sqlite3PagerFile, and sqlite3PagerJournalname expose three stable borrowed owners held by Pager: the VFS, the open database file handle, and the rollback-journal pathname.
excluded_responsibilities: User-visible filename normalization for memory databases
Selection between rollback-journal and WAL file handles
Lifetime management of returned borrowed owners

external_source_responsibilities: Pager.open constructs and Pager.close retires all three owners
dependencies.caller_closure: Each complete straight-line accessor and return block is assigned. Production Pager creation, I/O, file-control, journal open/delete, and public control paths consume the same fields.

outputs: Borrowed VFS pointer, borrowed open database sqlite3_file pointer, or borrowed sentinel-terminated rollback-journal pathname
contracts.ownership: Pager retains all ownership. Callers must not free or outlive Pager with any returned value.
contracts.state_and_results: Accessors return exact field identity without allocation, copying, dispatch, or mutation.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: No synchronization, callbacks, or I/O; caller owns any required Pager serialization.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Infallible for a live Pager. Returned values remain valid until Pager destruction.

representation_differences: The source database-file accessor documents a possible null result before file open. Production Zig publishes Pager only after a successful file open, so its live-Pager accessor returns a nonoptional pointer.
The journal pathname is a sentinel-terminated borrowed slice rather than a bare C pointer, preserving both length and C interoperability.

oracle.protocol: Open a Pager through a named ABI VFS, compare VFS and database-file pointer identity, compare the canonical journal pathname, use each owner through its native path, and close the Pager.
oracle.normalization: Pointers compare only for identity within one process; pathname bytes and sentinel are exact.

assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O or mutation; caller owns synchronization.
assurance.malformed_input: Only a live Pager is accepted by the typed API.
assurance.continuation: Access does not alter any Pager or owner state.

integration.native_call_path: Pager.open initializes abi_vfs, file, and journal_name; typed accessors expose those exact owners to B-tree, frontend, VFS-control, and diagnostic paths.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Callers no longer need direct field reach-through for these source accessor boundaries.

independent_review.notes: Requires caller migration, scoped durable trace promotion, and independent review.

known_blockers: Migrate appropriate direct field consumers to the typed Pager accessors.
Capture a scoped durable owner-identity receipt before internal-trace promotion.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/pager.c:7142-7176 complete VFS, database-file, journal-file adjacency, and journal-name accessors were reviewed
src/core/pager.zig Pager open, owner fields, journal transport, close paths, direct consumers, and identity tests were reviewed
callers: Frontend file-control and journal-file control paths
assertions_branches_cleanup: Each generated return block is assigned
No branches or cleanup belong to these accessors
upstream_tests: Upstream pager, VFS, backup, filename, file-control, and journal tests exercise these accessors
Project Pager and VFS suites exercise exact owner identity and lifetime
